Bollinger mean‑reversion trades are most profitable when executed in a sufficiently volatile regime; by requiring ATR above its 20‑period average we filter out flat periods that generate many false breakouts, while extreme RSI values confirm over‑bought/over‑sold conditions. This combination reduces over‑trading and aligns entries with price moves that are likely to revert.

Combining these with ATR‑based risk limits ensures that only trades in sufficiently volatile regimes are taken, reducing exposure to choppy periods and improving Sharpe.
